t: You're by the Thames, where the Skylon once stood. It was a slender, cigar-shaped steel tower, a tensegrity structure that seemed to float above the ground, built in 1951 for the Festival of Britain. It no longer exists here. Three people designed it. Hidalgo Moya, an American-born architect who worked mostly in England, and Philip Powell, an English post-war architect, shaped its look. Felix Samuely, an Austrian-British structural engineer, worked on the engineering side. Between them they made something that looked as though it shouldn't stay up.
